subject: Onboarding: regional capacity selection & autoscale/burst playbook
messages:
From: Chris Lang <chris@orbithealth.com>
To: rafael_mendes@redwood.com
Cc: procurement@orbithealth.com
Date: 2026-08-12T09:12:00-07:00
Subject: Re: Kickoff follow-up - capacity and burst questions

Rafael,

Thanks again for the call this morning. A few items we need clarified before procurement greenlights the SOW:

- Which regions are you recommending we initially reserve capacity in, given Orbit's primary user base in US-East and a small but growing presence in EU?
- What burst policy would we need to sign up for to cover a 3x traffic spike during our targeted launch window (expected 2 weeks after turnup)?
- Can you share a simple cost delta between a 24/7 reserved pool vs reserved + burst pool for the first 90 days?

Attaching our internal traffic matrix and a high-level launch plan. Can we get a written summary we can attach to the procurement packet?

Chris
Head of Platform Ops
Orbit Health

Attachments: orbit-traffic-matrix.csv (csv)
From: rafael_mendes@redwood.com
To: Chris Lang <chris@orbithealth.com>
Cc: kimberly_park@redwood.com, priya_natarajan@redwood.com, procurement@orbithealth.com
Date: 2026-08-12T12:03:00-07:00
Subject: Re: Kickoff follow-up - capacity and burst questions

Chris — thanks for the clear list. Below is a short summary you can drop into procurement; we also attached a formal runbook for technical owners. High-level answers first, then configurable knobs.

High-level recommendation (short):
- Initial regions: US-East primary (prod), US-West warm standby for latency and failover, EU-West as a cold pool (on-demand warm-up) given low EU traffic in month 1.
- Burst policy: reserve baseline throughput for 24/7 pool sized at your pre-launch QPS with a 2x guaranteed burst band and an on-demand burst multiplier (up to 4x) that draws on auto-provisioned capacity. We recommend committing to 2x in the SOW and enabling on-demand 3-4x for launch with additional notifications and spend caps.
- Cost delta (90 days): see attached region-capacity-matrix.xlsx — rough estimate: reserved-only baseline = $X; reserved + committed burst (2x) = +22% baseline; reserved + on-demand burst (up to 4x) = +22% baseline + consumption billing for additional tokens beyond committed band.

Configurable knobs we suggest for Orbit:
- commit_band: baseline GPU vCPU/RAM per pool (customer-defined)
- guaranteed_burst: 2x (SLA-backed)
- on_demand_multiplier: 3-4x (soft-limit, billing based)
- warm_standby_strategy: keep model weights pinned in US-West with warmed cache retention window of 30m before scale-down

Next steps / asks (action items):
1) Procurement: confirm you can sign SOW with 2x guaranteed burst and on-demand pass-through.
2) Orbit Ops: approve the region choices or suggest moving EU to warm standby if you expect EU spike earlier.
3) NetOps: provide any IP allowlist constraints for VPC peering.

I9ll loop Kim (network/ops) and Priya (CS implementation) on the technical playbook.

- Rafael
Director, Customer Success — Redwood Inference

Attachments referenced: orbit_onboarding_runbook_v1.pdf, region-capacity-matrix.xlsx, docusign-sow-link.txt
From: kimberly_park@redwood.com
To: Chris Lang <chris@orbithealth.com>, rafael_mendes@redwood.com
Cc: priya_natarajan@redwood.com
Date: 2026-08-13T08:45:00-07:00
Subject: Re: Kickoff follow-up - capacity and burst questions

Chris / Rafael — a couple of technical constraints and clarifications from NetOps: 

- If Orbit wants EU as a warm standby (fast failover), we should reserve a small baseline GPU pool in EU-West sized at ~15% of US-East baseline to keep model weights primed. Full warm standby (30m cache) will add ~8% to the monthly reserved cost compared to cold on-demand.
- Warm cache retention: 30m recommended for quick recoveries; if you accept longer spin-up (3-5m), we can move to a cold standby and save the warm cache cost.
- Autoscale policy suggestion: baseline autoscale policy with continuous batching and a 90th-percentile latency SLO of 120ms/response at baseline; scale thresholds: CPU/GPU metrics and token-latency increase trigger.

Operational checklist (short):
- Provide VPC CIDR ranges and peering window (preferred date)
- Share any data residency constraints for EU users
- Confirm SSO/KMS integration timeline if you need private deployment options

I9ve appended a short ops note to the runbook for your engineers. Happy to jump on a 30-minute technical sync once procurement signals green.

- Kim
Senior NetOps Engineer — Redwood Inference

Attachment: region-capacity-matrix.xlsx (updated with warm-standby line)
From: priya_natarajan@redwood.com
To: Chris Lang <chris@orbithealth.com>, kimberly_park@redwood.com, rafael_mendes@redwood.com
Date: 2026-08-13T14:10:00-07:00
Subject: Re: Kickoff follow-up - capacity and burst questions

Chris — adding implementation timeline and owner assignments for your packet. Please see the short MAP below that procurement can include: 

Implementation MAP (90-day window):
- Week 0 (procurement & SOW): sign SOW with 2x guaranteed burst band, attach region choices (US-East, US-West, EU-West cold). Owner: Procurement (Orbit).
- Week 1-2 (network & secrets): VPC peering, IP allowlist, KMS key exchange. Owner: Orbit NetOps; Redwood NetOps (Kim) assigned.
- Week 2-3 (pilot turnup): provision reserved pool in US-East; enable warm standby in US-West (minimal baseline). Owner: Redwood CS (Priya).
- Week 4-6 (validation): run load tests against pilot, validate autoscale triggers, and exercise a 3x burst simulation. Owner: Orbit Platform + Redwood Ops.
- Week 6-12 (ramp to prod): expand reserved baseline as needed, enable on-demand burst during launch window with spend caps; handover to Orbit SREs. Owner: Orbit SRE + Redwood CS.

Minimum SOW language we recommend (one paragraph):
Redwood will provide a dedicated GPU pool in US-East for Orbit Health with a guaranteed 2x committed burst band and the option to consume on-demand burst capacity up to 4x of baseline. Redwood will maintain region-specific warm-standby options and collaborate on network peering and KMS integrations; claims and costs for on-demand burst beyond the committed band will be billed per consumption rates outlined in Exhibit B.

Action items for Orbit procurement (we can supply boilerplate text):
- Confirm signatory and procurement ETA (date)
- Confirm whether EU-West should be warm standby or cold on-demand
- Approve the spend cap for on-demand burst during the 2-week launch window (suggested default: $25k)

If you confirm the above I9ll schedule the pilot provisioning for Week 2.

- Priya
Technical Implementation Lead — Redwood Inference
From: Chris Lang <chris@orbithealth.com>
To: rafael_mendes@redwood.com, priya_natarajan@redwood.com, kimberly_park@redwood.com
Cc: procurement@orbithealth.com, monica_patel@redwood.com

Subject: Re: Kickoff follow-up - capacity and burst questions

Rafael / Priya / Kim — thanks for the fast turnaround and the write-up. Procurement approved the SOW with the 2x guaranteed burst line and the suggested $25k spend cap for the launch window. We9ll keep EU-West as cold on-demand for now and revisit after M1 metrics.

Next steps from Orbit:
- Procurement will route the SOW to our legal signatory by EOD Monday (we9ll include the runbook as an exhibit).
- NetOps will send VPC CIDR and peering window by Tuesday.

Please schedule the Week 2 pilot provisioning for Wed Aug 26 (we prefer morning PST). Monica, could you confirm Redwood9s provisioning lead and the estimated time to have the US-East pool ready once we9ve completed peering?

Chris
